config.title: Dog Parks in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Where the leash rule stops, how big the forest areas and fenced runs are, what dogs may never enter, and what registration and tax cost.

items.q: Is there a leash law in Berlin?
items.a: Yes. The Berlin dog law (HundeG) took effect on **22 July 2016** and the general leash rule has applied across the city since **1 January 2019**. Dogs may run free only inside the marked forest dog areas and the fenced runs. Two groups are exempt from the general rule: a **Bestandshund** kept by the same holder since before 22 July 2016, and a dog whose owner holds a **Sachkundenachweis**. Even those dogs stay on the lead in parks, on unmarked forest paths, in shops, on public transport and in pedestrian zones.

items.q: How long can the leash be in Berlin?
items.a: The law caps it at **two metres** in parks, green spaces and forests and at **one metre** in pedestrian zones, shops, public buildings, stations and on public transport. A long training line in a Volkspark is a fine waiting to happen.

items.q: Where can dogs run off the leash in Berlin?
items.a: In the **twelve forest areas** run by Berliner Forsten, about **1,220 hectares** in total: Grunewald, Wannsee-Düppel, Düppel, Kladow, Pichelswerder, Hakenfelde, Jungfernheide, Frohnau and Blankenfelde. And in the **fenced runs** the districts set up in parks, such as Stralauer Platz, Volkspark Friedrichshain, Gleisdreieck, Volkspark Jungfernheide, the three runs on Tempelhofer Feld and Hasenheide. Everywhere else the lead stays on.

items.q: Which Berlin dog areas are fenced?
items.a: The park runs are. Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg publishes nine between **1,160 and 2,900 m²**; Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf four, the biggest in Volkspark Jungfernheide at about 9,200 m²; Reinickendorf eight Hundegärten; Steglitz-Zehlendorf one at Barnackufer. Fence heights differ: **Stralauer Platz has 1.40 m** and is marked as suitable for big dogs, **Wriezener Park and Weidenweg have 0.80 m**. The forest areas are not fenced at all, so they need a dog that comes back.

items.q: Are dogs allowed at Berlin lakes and beaches?
items.a: Not at public bathing spots. The dog law bans dogs from **playgrounds, Badeanstalten, public Badestellen and marked sunbathing lawns**. Inside a forest dog area the Forsten ask that dogs do not run free or swim where people bathe in the warm months, and marked nature reserves and fenced plots are excluded from the area entirely. A few marked Hundebadestellen exist; the sign on site decides.

items.q: What does it cost to register a dog in Berlin?
items.a: Registration in the **Hunderegister is €17.50 online** and €26.50 by post or phone, due as soon as you keep the dog in Berlin, with the 15-digit chip number. Since 1 January 2024 that registration is also the tax registration. **Hundesteuer is €120 a year for the first dog and €180 for each further dog.** Liability insurance and a microchip are mandatory. Not registering can cost up to €10,000.

items.q: How do I get a leash exemption in Berlin?
items.a: Apply at your district Ordnungsamt for the **Befreiung von der Leinenpflicht**. You need liability insurance, the chip number, a photo and proof of Sachkunde: either three years of trouble-free dog keeping within the last five, or the official exam. The fee is **€20.50 per quarter hour of processing, up to €164**. The exemption lifts the general rule only; parks, forests outside the dog areas, transport and pedestrian zones still require the lead.

items.q: What is the fine for a dog off the leash in Berlin?
items.a: The law allows fines **up to €10,000**. In practice Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg says a first offence is usually a **€45 warning**, with up to €5,000 possible for repeat cases. Not picking up after the dog is fined separately.
